counterparts.title: The term sheet
openers: So. Convince me this is the round I should be in.
I've read the deck twice. Tell me what isn't in it.
We can sign this week. Or we can not. Talk to me.
Before the numbers — why you, and why now?

wants.name: Traction
wants.tell: They keep glancing back at your weekly numbers.
wants.reveal: They want one line going up and to the right. Everything else is decoration.
wants.hit: “That's the line I came to see. Say the number again.”

wants.name: A moat
wants.tell: Every question they ask ends with “and what stops anyone else?”
wants.reveal: They aren't worried you'll fail. They're worried you'll be copied by Christmas.
wants.hit: “Okay. That's actually hard to copy. Go on.”

wants.name: You
wants.tell: They keep steering the conversation away from the product and back to you.
wants.reveal: They've decided the market's fine. They're underwriting the founder.
wants.hit: “I back people. You just made that easy.”

wants.name: Discipline
wants.tell: They asked what you burned last month before they asked what you built.
wants.reveal: They've been burned by founders who spend a round in a year.
wants.hit: “Good. I hate paying for other people's optimism.”

land: They laugh, properly, and put the phone face down.
“I came through your part of town this morning. It's changed.”
The small talk goes on a minute longer than it needed to. That's good.
“You're the third meeting today and the first one I've enjoyed.”
“Right — so you already know where the hard part is.”
They stop taking notes and start arguing with you, which is better.
“Most people in that chair can't answer that.”
They redraw your architecture on the napkin and get it right.
miss: “Hm.” They write one word down and underline it.
“I don't think that's how that market works.”
You hear yourself over-explaining. So do they.
“Let's come back to that.” They don't come back to it.

land: They talk about the fund for four minutes. You learn more than in the deck.
“Honestly? I'm bored of the last six companies I saw.”
They tell you about the one they passed on. It still stings.
“Nobody asks me that.” They sit back.
“Okay. Okay. Say that to my partners on Thursday.”
They're doing arithmetic in the margin and it's coming out well.
“I think I want more of this than the paper says.”
They pick the term sheet up. That's the first time they've touched it.
miss: “That's a slide, not an answer.”
They check the time in a way you're supposed to see.
“Everyone says that. What do you say?”
The number you led with is now the number they're negotiating down.

closings.hostile: They leave the paper on the table like it's already withdrawn.
closings.cool: They'll sign it, but they've taken a red pen to it.
closings.even: The terms are the terms. Nobody moved.
closings.warm: They've marked the sheet up in your favour and initialled it.
closings.sold: “I'll take less of it and pay more for it. Don't make me regret this.”

counterparts.title: The client meeting
openers: We've read the brief. Talk us through the work.
Two other studios quoted us. Why are we still sitting here?
Be honest about the date and we'll be honest about the budget.
Last agency shipped us a demo and called it a product. Convince us.

wants.name: Certainty
wants.tell: They asked twice about the date before they asked about the money.
wants.reveal: They've been burned by a late delivery and will not be burned twice.
wants.hit: “Good. Put that date in writing and we're done.”

wants.name: Craft
wants.tell: They keep pulling up screenshots of things they think are beautiful.
wants.reveal: Their board judges them on how it looks. It has to look expensive.
wants.hit: “That's the standard. That's exactly the standard.”

wants.name: Their budget
wants.tell: Every number you say, they repeat back slightly smaller.
wants.reveal: The money is fixed and the person who fixed it isn't in the room.
wants.hit: “If you can live inside that, we can sign today.”

wants.name: A partner
wants.tell: They keep saying “we” about work you haven't started.
wants.reveal: They don't want a supplier. They want somebody who'll still take the call in a year.
wants.hit: “I'd rather work with people than vendors.”

land: The room warms up by about a degree, which is a lot for a room like this.
“We drove past your office. Smaller than we expected — in a good way.”
Somebody makes a joke about procurement and everybody means it.
The coffee arrives and nobody looks at their laptop for a while.
“You've clearly done this before.”
They ask a technical question to catch you out. You answer it.
“That's the first time anyone's explained that to us properly.”
Their engineer stops taking notes and starts nodding.
miss: “That sounds like a lot of maybe.”
Their engineer writes something down and shows it to their boss.
You quote a number and immediately hedge it. They noticed.
“We've heard that estimate before, from the last people.”

land: They tell you what actually went wrong last time. It's worse than the brief said.
“Off the record — this project is somebody's job.”
Ten minutes about their real problem, and none of it was in the brief.
“Nobody's asked us what we want since we started this.”
“That's the version we wanted and couldn't describe.”
They start talking about phase two, which means there's a phase one.
“Okay — what would it take to start Monday?”
Somebody quietly moves the meeting's end time back.
miss: “That's more than we asked for and more than we'll pay for.”
They look at each other. Nobody looks at you.
“We're not sure that's the same project any more.”
The word “scope” gets said twice and it isn't a compliment.

closings.hostile: They'll take the quote to a competitor, and they'll say so.
closings.cool: They'll sign, but they've shaved the fee and moved the date in.
closings.even: The job is the job as written.
closings.warm: They've found a little more money and a little more time.
closings.sold: “We'll pay properly for people who talk like that.”

counterparts.title: The interview
openers: Twenty minutes, on the record. Why does this exist?
I've got a slot on Friday. Give me a reason to fill it with you.
Everyone's shipping this week. What makes yours the one I write about?
I'm going to ask you the mean question at the end. Fair warning.

wants.name: A story
wants.tell: They stopped taking notes and started listening.
wants.reveal: They don't want the feature list. They want the reason you started.
wants.hit: “Say that again — slower. That's the opening paragraph.”

wants.name: An angle
wants.tell: They keep asking about everybody else's product, not yours.
wants.reveal: They're writing about the category. You're either the example or the footnote.
wants.hit: “That's the trend piece. You just gave me the trend piece.”

wants.name: Candour
wants.tell: They wince, very slightly, every time you say “excited to announce”.
wants.reveal: They've heard four launch pitches today and can smell a press release.

wants.name: Something first
wants.tell: They ask, twice, who else you've spoken to.
wants.reveal: They want a number nobody else has printed yet.
wants.hit: “Is that on the record? Say yes. Say yes.”

land: They put the recorder down for a second, which is when the good quotes happen.
“God, this industry. Sorry — go on.”
You get four minutes of them complaining about embargoes. It's a good sign.
“You're the only founder today who hasn't said ‘disrupt’.”
“How do you spell that? I'm using it.”
They ask a follow-up that means they understood the first answer.
“That's the bit nobody else in this category will say out loud.”
The recorder gets nudged an inch closer to you.
miss: “That's the same line as everyone else's press release.”
They stop writing. They don't start again.
“I'll be honest, my readers won't care about that.”
“So it's a feature, then, not a product.”

land: They tell you the piece they actually want to write. It's better than the one you pitched.
“I've been on this beat six years. It's mostly noise.”
They tell you who else is launching this week. That's a gift.
“Off the record, I already know how this story ends. Prove me wrong.”
“That's the headline. I'm not even going to rewrite it.”
They read the quote back to you to check they've got it exactly.
“I'll move you up the page for that.”
“Okay, that's a story. That's a real story.”
miss: “That's marketing. I don't print marketing.”
They circle something on the page. It's not a compliment.
“You realise I have to write what actually shipped.”
“I'll put it in the round-up.” The round-up is where things go to die.

closings.hostile: They've got their angle now, and it isn't yours.
closings.cool: You'll get a paragraph. A cautious one.
closings.even: They'll write what they were always going to write.
closings.warm: They're writing the good version, with your quote in it.
closings.sold: “This is the lead. Don't talk to anyone else before Friday.”

counterparts.title: The board room
openers: The quarter's in front of us. Explain it.
We've all read the pack. Let's talk about what isn't in it.
Nobody's here to shout. We're here to decide whether to keep waiting.
You've had our patience for a while now. Where has it gone?

wants.name: A plan
wants.tell: They keep steering you off this quarter and onto next one.
wants.reveal: They aren't angry about the miss. They're angry about the silence after it.
wants.hit: “Fine. Hold yourself to that and we'll hold off.”

wants.name: Ownership
wants.tell: Every time you say “the market” somebody's pen stops.
wants.reveal: They want to hear you say it was your call and it was wrong.
wants.hit: “Thank you. That's the first straight answer this year.”

wants.name: Focus
wants.tell: They list your projects back to you, slowly, one by one.
wants.reveal: They think you're doing four things badly instead of one thing well.
wants.hit: “One thing. Say it again so it's in the minutes.”

wants.name: To be in the room
wants.tell: They mention, twice, that they found out about the last decision by email.
wants.reveal: They don't want control. They want to not be surprised.
wants.hit: “We just want to hear it from you first. That's all.”

land: The temperature in the room drops a couple of degrees, which is the right direction.
Somebody asks about your holiday. It is not a trap.
“How are you, actually?” It's the first honest question of the meeting.
The chair closes the pack. That's the good version of closing the pack.
“That's the first number in this pack that means anything.”
You walk them through the mechanism and two of them start nodding.
“Okay. So you do know where the money went.”
Somebody writes down your date and reads it back.
miss: “That's an explanation, not an answer.”
“You said something similar last quarter.” Somebody finds the minutes.
The chair takes off their glasses. Nothing good follows that.
“I'm not sure you know why that happened either.”

land: They tell you what they're actually worried about. It isn't what they've been asking about.
“We've all run companies. We know what this feels like.”
One of them talks for five minutes about their own bad year.
“We'd rather hear the problem early than the excuse late.”
“That's a company. Go and run it.”
The chair looks around the table and nobody objects.
“We'll give you the two quarters. Don't come back with this again.”
Somebody moves that the item is closed. It carries.
miss: “We've heard the vision. We wanted the numbers.”
“You're pitching us. We're already in.”
The chair writes a single word and turns the page over.
“That's what you said in March.”

closings.hostile: They've moved from disappointed to organised, which is worse.
closings.cool: The item stays open. They'll want a plan in writing.
closings.even: The minutes will say the board noted it.
closings.warm: They've given you room. Not much, but room.
closings.sold: “We're behind you. Go and prove us right.”
